deck.title: Native Korean numbers
deck.goal: Recognize native forms and select shortened counter forms.

entries.usageNote: Before a counter, exactly 20 is 스무 rather than 스물.
Before counters, final 하나 becomes 한.

deck.title: Sino-Korean numbers
deck.goal: Read prices, dates and minutes in the Sino number system.

entries.usageNote: 영 is common in temperatures, math and measurements.
Often used when reading phone numbers or individual digits.

deck.title: Counters and classifiers
deck.goal: Select lexical counters and appropriate number forms in noun phrases.

entries.usageNote: Neutral people counter; 분 is a respectful variant.
Not the same use as 분 meaning minute.
Ordinarily uses Sino-Korean numbers, unlike many other counters.
Uses native numbers; 20 before 살 is 스무.
Native counting often applies to durations.
Uses Sino-Korean numbers for this counter.

deck.title: Calendar and dates
deck.goal: Recognize weekdays, date expressions and irregular month readings.

usageExample.english: We leave the day after tomorrow.
I met a friend the day before yesterday.

entries.usageNote: Sino-Korean number readings are used when reading years.
Month counting is a lexical calendar topic.
Context distinguishes the day marker from Sino 일 meaning one.

deck.title: Time expressions
deck.goal: Understand common clock forms, AM/PM and everyday schedules.

usageExample.english: I wake up in the morning.

deck.title: Prices, amounts and age
deck.goal: Handle everyday money and age phrases without counting them as grammar.

usageExample.english: The baby is one year old.

entries.usageNote: Age questions depend on social context; be considerate.

deck.title: Question and indefinite words
deck.goal: Acquire question and indefinite expressions separately from grammar rules.

usageExample.english: What kind of movie is it?
What sort of books do you like?

entries.usageNote: Requires a negative predicate for the 'nobody' reading.
Normally pairs with a negative predicate.
